title: GPU: require Vulkan for native rendering and compute
body:
Closes #712. Native rendering and GPU compute now use Vulkan exclusively, following the owner decision to retire D3D support. #561 and #708 are closed as superseded.

The desktop viewport, headless pictures, fluid solver and mesh GPU device share the Vulkan-only selection policy. `WGPU_BACKEND=dx12`, `metal` or `gl` returns an actionable Vulkan error; mixed backend lists can only select Vulkan. Headless automatic rendering retains its CPU fallback, and strict hardware/software requests still require the requested Vulkan tier. The shared Vulkan instance and solver device/pipeline reuse remain intact.

Remove native DX12/Metal/GL features, DXC/FXC compiler handling and the GL fallback. Disable egui-wgpu defaults and use eframe's `wgpu_no_default_features` so dependency feature unification cannot silently restore those native backends. Browser dependencies explicitly retain WebGPU/WebGL and wasm handle support. Apple targets explicitly enable Vulkan portability. Linux package metadata now requires the Vulkan loader rather than accepting EGL as an alternative. Update support docs, contributor/agent guidance and the roadmap; preserve historical Metal measurements labelled as historical.

**Platform impact:** the native viewport requires Vulkan. The macOS package does not bundle a Vulkan portability implementation; stock macOS without a separate installation cannot open the native viewport. CPU CLI solves and CPU snapshots remain available. This path needs macOS runtime verification before release.

WGSL instructions and solver numerics are unchanged; the shader edit is a comment cleanup. This does not implement fan/porous zones, buffer splitting or two-fluid coupling.

## Validation

- `cargo check -p fieldcraft -p fieldcraft-gpu -p fieldcraft-lbm-gpu`; native app/CLI builds: pass.
- Normal `fieldcraft`, `fieldcraft-gpu`, `fieldcraft-lbm-gpu`, `fieldcraft-mesh-gpu` and `fieldcraft-ui-egui` suites on software Vulkan with `FIELDCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU=1`: pass, including 22 fluid verification cases, mesh CPU/GPU agreement, 186 UI tests and doc tests. CLI tests: 3 pass (selected with the native app packages to keep the same unified dependency features).
- Added policy regressions: compiled native backends are exactly Vulkan; overrides cannot enable another backend; instance reuse remains intact. All five policy tests pass with obsolete `WGPU_DX12_COMPILER=staticdxc` set.
- Targeted `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` for all six touched crates/packages: pass (`fieldcraft`, `fieldcraft-cli`, `fieldcraft-web`, `fieldcraft-gpu`, `fieldcraft-lbm-gpu`, `fieldcraft-ui-egui`).
- Targeted wasm check for the web app, GPU, fluid GPU and UI crates: pass. Windows MSVC cross-check for GPU/fluid GPU: pass. Linux/Windows/macOS feature graphs show only Vulkan (plus explicit Apple Vulkan portability); the web graph retains WebGPU/WebGL.
- Native Xvfb window: reports Vulkan, completes the heated-flow GPU solve and captures the results view with the obsolete DXC override set. DX12-only desktop startup is refused; CLI CPU/auto snapshots still work under that override, while a strict software-GPU snapshot refuses it. The Xvfb run uses process-local library paths for this host's Homebrew runtime.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `git diff --check`, `cargo xtask assets` (377 attributed files), `layers` (23 crates) and `unit-factors`: pass.

## Known limitations

- No hardware GPU is available on this host. The native window and GPU solve smoke checks use Mesa lavapipe/llvmpipe, LLVM 21.1.8, through Vulkan. Windows validation is cross-compilation and feature-graph inspection; no Windows runtime or hardware performance claim is made.
- macOS Vulkan portability is enabled in the feature graph but has not been built or run here. Loader/driver installation is external; no MoltenVK distribution or automatic setup is added.
- The heated-flow sample is only a path smoke test: a 45 s transient over a held-temperature bracket, not a steady or coupled exchanger validation. Its existing compressibility warning remains visible. No new physical-accuracy or release-completeness claim is made.
- Ignored heavy benchmarks and the full CI gate are left to upstream CI; no local `cargo xtask ci`, workspace clippy or oracle regeneration was run because numerical behavior is unchanged.
